newsitem.title: MEXICO: Some Mexico workers seen keeping govt pension plan.
newsitem.headline: Some Mexico workers seen keeping govt pension plan.

text.p: Between two and three million workers will likely maintain their pension plans with the Mexican government instead of switching to private plans, an industry leader said Tuesday.

Ralf Peters, president of the Mexican Association of Administrators of Retirement Funds (Amafores), said in an interview in Reforma newspaper that many workers will keep their plan with Bank of Mexico's Consolidated Account.

Those workers, he said, have not had any contact with any of the new private pension funds, or Afores, or else they have not made a final decision to join any of funds, which start operating on July 1.

"The first of July we estimate that there are going to be four or five million workers affiliated (with the new Afores), but the key moment is going to be September 17, when they receive their first contribution.
"I would say that then we will have six to seven million workers affiliated and two to three (million) who fall into the Consolidated Account," Peters was quoted as saying.
